question: The shape of the voltage-current graph for a conductor is ______.
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Linear curve**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The current-voltage graph of ohmic devices is of the form linear curve.
 
• **Ohm’s Law**
 
 
• The **electric current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends.**
 
• It is given by the formula:
 
• **V=IR**
 
 
 
• The **device which follows ohm's law** for all voltages across it is called an **ohmic device.**
 
• The current-voltage graph of ohmic devices is a** linear curve.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1529a72d4df18ab6810383e32f6b80e0aa2ce8a7c0d65a90cbb81bb761c4c7b0.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c32605285426d15682332d013cdd043a12b87785e1ad56c47c6ae2a1b70b6a88.png] **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zig-Zag**:

 
 
• This **type of graph suggests a non-smooth, alternating pattern**.
 
• While some materials, **such as semiconductors or conductors under varying external conditions, might exhibit irregularities in their behaviour**,
 
• It is **more associated with irregular, fluctuating behaviours**
 
 
 
• **Parabolic**:
 
 
• A** parabolic graph suggests that the relationship between voltage and current is quadratic**.
 
• This can occur in** certain non-ohmic materials, where the resistance is not constant but changes with the applied voltage. **
 
• **For example,** in materials like diodes or thermistors (at higher voltages), the current may increase more rapidly than the voltage, resulting in a parabolic relationship.
 
• This is **often seen in semiconductor devices**
 
 
 
• **Exponential**:
 
 
• An exponential relationship **indicates that the current increases (or decreases) exponentially with voltage**.
 
• This type of behaviour is typical in certain non-linear devices, like **diodes** or **transistors**.
 
• In **these devices, small changes in voltage lead to large changes in current, especially when they are forward-biased.**
 
• The voltage-current graph in such cases often has an exponential shape.
